```json
    "title": "Note",
    "entry": "note/index.html",
    "mode": "detached",
    "frame": { "x": 120, "y": 120, "width": 240, "height": 200 },
    "minSize": { "width": 160, "height": 120 }
  },
  {
    "id": "pet",
    "entry": "pet/index.html",
    "mode": "detached",
    "chrome": "none",
    "clickThrough": true,
    "resizable": false,
    "frame": { "x": 40, "y": 500, "width": 96, "height": 96 }
  }
]
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `frame` | `{ x, y, width, height }` where it first opens, from the window's top left corner, in the page's CSS pixels. Any part can be left out. |
| `minSize`, `maxSize` | `{ width, height }` limits for resizing. The smallest default is 24 × 24. |
| `chrome` | `standard` (default) draws a card with a header that moves it. `none` draws nothing: the page fills the frame. |
| `transparent` | Nothing is drawn behind the page, so what is under it shows where the page is transparent, such as around rounded corners. On by default with `chrome: "none"`, off otherwise. Give the page `background: transparent`. Fixed once the panel opens. |
| `clickThrough` | Clicks pass through the panel to what is under it, except over its [hit regions](#clicks-and-dragging). |
| `movable`, `resizable` | Whether the user can move it by its header or drag regions, and resize it by its edges and corners. Both default to `true`. |
| `scope` | `global` (default) shows it in every project. `project` shows it only in one project, and keeps it alive, hidden, while you are elsewhere. That is the project it was opened in; opening it again, or setting `scope: "project"`, moves it to the current one. |

Every field above is a default. An extension can change all of them while the
panel is open, except `transparent`.

- The frame is fitted inside the window, and moved back in when the window
  shrinks. With `chrome: "standard"`, the header takes the top of the frame.
- Muxy remembers where the user leaves a panel opened without an instance name.
  Instances are the extension's to remember, with `onChange` below.
- An extension keeps at most 32 panels open, docked and detached together.

### Instances

Open one panel several times by naming each copy. Each instance has its own
page, data, frame, and options.

```js
await muxy.panels.open("note", { text: "" }, { instance: "note-3", frame: { x: 300, y: 80 } });
await muxy.panels.update("note", { title: "Groceries" }, "note-3");
await muxy.panels.close("note", "note-3");
const open = await muxy.panels.list();
```

An instance name is 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, or `-`. A page reads its
own as `muxy.panel.instanceID`, and `lifecycle.onBeforeClose` handlers get it as
`panelInstanceID`. `panel.opened` and `panel.closed` [events](events.md) carry it
as `instance`. `list()` returns the extension's open panels: docked ones, and
detached ones even while another project hides them. A named copy that another
docked panel replaces is closed.

### Options

`open`, `toggle`, `update`, and `muxy.panel.update` take the same options.
Fields left out keep their current value.

| Option | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `instance` | Which copy to open (in `open` and `toggle`). |
| `mode` | `pinned`, `floating`, or `detached`. Moves an open panel between docked and detached. |
| `position` | `right` or `bottom`, where it docks. |
| `frame` | `{ x, y, width, height }`, any part. |
| `minSize`, `maxSize` | `{ width, height }` |
| `chrome`, `clickThrough`, `movable`, `resizable`, `scope` | As in the manifest. |
| `transparent` | Only when the instance opens. |
| `title` | The header title; `null` clears it. |
| `hiddenControls` | Replaces the manifest's list. |
| `hitRegions` | Rectangles where the page takes clicks. `null` removes them: the page then takes clicks everywhere, or nowhere while `clickThrough` is on. |
| `dragRegions` | Rectangles that move the panel when dragged. |

### From the panel itself

A panel page controls its own panel with `muxy.panel`. It is `null` on other
pages.

```js
muxy.panel.setFrame({ width: 320, height: 140 });       // grow to show a speech bubble
muxy.panel.setOptions({ chrome: "none", movable: true });
muxy.panel.setDragRegions([{ x: 0, y: 0, width: 96, height: 96 }]);
muxy.panel.raise();
muxy.panel.onChange(state => save(state.frame));
```

| Member | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `instanceID` | This copy's instance name, or `null` |
| `update(options)`, `setOptions(options)` | Changes any [option](#options) |
| `setFrame(frame)`, `setTitle(title)` | Shortcuts for `update` |
| `setHitRegions(rects)`, `setDragRegions(rects)` | See below |
| `trackHitElements(target, { padding, interval })` | Keeps the hit regions on elements as they move and resize. `target` is a CSS selector, an element, a list, or a function returning elements. Returns a function that stops tracking. |
| `raise()` | Brings the panel to the front |
| `get()`, `state` | The panel's state, below |
| `onChange(fn)` | Called with the new state whenever it changes, such as after the user moves it or the window resizes |

The state is `{ panelID, instance, mode, position, visible, frame, bounds,
scope, chrome, transparent, clickThrough, movable, resizable, title, focused }`.
`bounds` is the window's `{ width, height }`, the space a detached panel can
use.

### Clicks and dragging

Rectangles are in the page's CSS pixels, from its top left corner.

- **Hit regions.** With `clickThrough`, or once hit regions are set, the page
  takes clicks only inside its hit regions. Everywhere else, clicks and scrolling
  reach the terminal, tab, or panel underneath. A pet sets its hit region to
  its body, and to its speech bubble while one shows.
- **Drag regions.** Dragging inside one moves the panel. A frameless panel uses
  them as its handle. The page doesn't get those clicks.

```js
// A pet that wanders, and can be clicked and dragged.
const pet = document.querySelector("#pet");
muxy.panel.trackHitElements("#pet, .bubble");
muxy.panel.setDragRegions([{ x: 0, y: 0, width: 96, height: 96 }]);
pet.addEventListener("click", async () => {
  const { frame } = await muxy.panel.get();
  await muxy.panel.setFrame({ width: 280, height: frame.height + 80, y: frame.y - 80 });
  showBubble("Hi!");
});
```

## Popovers

A popover opens under a top bar item, left of a rail item, or above a status
bar item, and closes when you click outside it.

```json
"popovers": [{ "id": "status", "entry": "status/index.html", "width": 320, "height": 360 }],
"commands": [{ "id": "show-status", "title": "Status", "action": { "kind": "openPopover", "popover": "status" } }],
"statusBarItems": [{ "id": "status", "icon": "bolt", "side": "right", "command": "show-status" }]
```

- Popovers open only from bar items whose command uses `openPopover`. Needs
  `panels:write`.
- `width` and `height` default to 320 × 360. `muxy.popover.resize(w, h)`
  changes them within 80–600 × 80–720.
- `muxy.popover.close()` closes it.

## Sidebar

An extension can provide one full-height page that replaces the built-in
sidebar.

```json
"sidebar": { "id": "main", "title": "My Sidebar", "icon": "sidebar.left", "entry": "sidebar/index.html" }
```

Users turn it on in **Settings → Appearance → Active sidebar**, which lists the
built-in sidebar and every enabled extension that declares one. If the chosen
extension is disabled or removed, the built-in sidebar shows until it returns.
It can't close itself. The manifest and the choice carry over from Muxy 1.x
unchanged.

# Permissions

An extension lists what it needs in `muxy.permissions`. Calls without the
matching permission fail, and unknown permission names stop the extension from
loading. Ask for the minimum.

```json
"permissions": ["tabs:read", "git:read", "notifications:write"]
```

## Permissions

| Permission | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `tabs:read` | `tabs.list` |
| `tabs:write` | Open, switch, split, create, close, rename, color, pin, and move tabs; set a tab's title and icon; `openTab` commands |
| `panes:read` | `panes.list`, `panes.readScreen` |
| `panes:write` | Every other `panes.*` call: typing, closing, focusing, splitting, zooming, detaching, restarting, floating, and moving panes |
| `projects:read` | List projects, workspaces, and removed projects; the `projects.changed` event |
| `projects:write` | Add, switch, rename, recolor, reorder, focus, sort, and restore projects; manage workspaces |
| `projects:delete` | `projects.delete` |
| `worktrees:read` | `worktrees.list`; the `worktree.headChanged` event |
| `worktrees:write` | `worktrees.switchTo`, `worktrees.refresh` |
| `agents:read` | `agents.list`; the `agent.status` event |
| `agents:write` | `agents.focus` |
| `files:read` | `files.list`, `files.read`, `files.stat`; the `file.changed` event |
| `files:write` | `files.write`, `mkdir`, `rename`, `move`, `delete` |
| `git:read` | Status, diffs, log, branches, worktrees, pull request info |
| `git:write` | Every other `git.*` call |
| `gh:read` | `gh.user` |
| `storage:read` / `storage:write` | Read / change the extension's storage |
| `notifications:write` | `notifications.notify`, `toast` |
| `panels:write` | Panels, popovers, modal web views, and setting bar items; panel, popover, and modal commands |
| `commands:run-script` | `runScript` commands |
| `commands:exec` | `exec`, `execAsync` |
| `shortcuts:register` | `shortcuts.register`, `shortcuts.unregister` |
| `browser:read` / `browser:write` | Read / drive [browser tabs](../features/browser.md) with `muxy.browser` |
| `ui:write` | Every `ui.*` call but `ui.state`: panels, layout, the command palette, Settings, history, floats, and the Quick Terminal |
| `commands:read` / `commands:run` | `commands.list` / `commands.run` |
| `composer:write` | `composer.*` |
| `layouts:read` / `layouts:write` | `layouts.list` / `layouts.apply` |
| `preferences:read` | `preferences.get`, `preferences.themes`; the `preferences.changed` event |
| `preferences:write` | `preferences.set` |
| `clipboard:read` / `clipboard:write` | `clipboard.readText` / `clipboard.writeText` |
| `system:open` | `projects.apps`, `projects.openIn`, `projects.reveal`, `app.openExternal` |
| `remote:serve` | Accepted; remote methods are not available in 2.x |

`http.fetch`, dialogs, the picker, `events`, `lifecycle`, `app.info`,
`ui.state`, and the extension's own `settings` need no permission.

## Runtime prompts

Some calls also ask the user each time, even with the permission:

| Asks before | Remembered per |
| --- | --- |
| Running a program (`exec`, `execAsync`) | Program, or shell command |
| Typing or pressing keys in a terminal, or sending the composer | Extension |
| Reading terminal output | Extension |
| Opening a terminal tab that runs a command, or running a custom command | Command |
| Opening another extension's tab | Extension |
| Changing the repository (`git:write` calls) | Operation |
| Changing files (`files:write` calls) | Operation |
| A web request (`http.fetch`) | Host |
| Deleting a project | Project |
| Reading the clipboard | Extension |

The user can **Allow** once, **Allow & Remember**, **Cancel**, **Deny &
Remember**, or block that kind of action for the extension. An unanswered
prompt is denied after 60 seconds, and at most five prompts can wait at once.
The extension's log notes each call that waits for an answer and each one
denied because nobody answered, and `muxy extension status` counts the
prompts still waiting.

The red **Always Allow This Extension…** button trusts the extension with
every action above, after a second warning confirms it. A trusted extension is
never prompted, and its saved rules, including Deny and Block, don't apply
until trust is removed. Cancelling the warning returns to the prompt.

Saved choices are listed under **Permission rules** on the extension's page in
**Settings → Extensions**, with **Reveal audit log** for a history of
decisions. **Always Allow…** there trusts the extension after the same warning,
and **Stop Always Allowing** removes the trust. **Clear all** and uninstalling
clear the rules and the trust.

# Tabs

A tab type is a web page that opens as a tab, next to terminal tabs. It can be
split, moved, and pinned like any tab, and is restored on launch.

```json
"tabTypes": [
  { "id": "viewer", "title": "Viewer", "entry": "viewer/index.html", "defaultData": { "mode": "list" } }
]
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Unique within the extension. |
| `title` | The tab's default title. |
| `entry` | HTML page in the extension folder. |
| `defaultData` | Data used when the tab is opened without any. |

Open a tab type from a [command](commands.md) with the `openTab` action, or
from code.

## Opening tabs

`tabs.open` needs `tabs:write` and returns the new tab's ID.

```js
// a page from this or another extension
await muxy.tabs.open({
  kind: "extensionWebView",
  extension: { id: "hello", tabType: "viewer", data: { mode: "grid" }, singleton: true },
});

// a terminal in the current project, optionally in a subfolder or running a command
await muxy.tabs.open({ kind: "terminal", directory: "src", command: "npm test" });

// a browser tab; drive it with muxy.browser
await muxy.tabs.open({ kind: "browser", url: "localhost:3000" });
```

- `singleton: true` focuses an existing tab of that type instead of opening
  another.
- Running a command, or opening another extension's tab, asks the user first.
- A terminal's `directory` must be a folder inside the current project, and
  works for local projects only.

## Tab groups

Tab groups show several of a project's tabs side by side. `tabs.split` does
what dragging a tab to an edge does: it moves the tab into a new group beside
the group showing another tab, and focuses it. Both tabs must belong to the
current project.

```js
const left = await muxy.tabs.open({ kind: "terminal" });
const right = await muxy.tabs.open({ kind: "terminal", directory: "server" });
await muxy.tabs.split(right, left, "right");
// opened next: joins the focused group, on the right
await muxy.tabs.open({ kind: "terminal", directory: "web" });
```

`edge` is `left`, `right` (default), `up`, or `down`. A group's only tab can't
split off beside its own group.

## Page data

Each tab has its own `data`, saved with the tab.

```js
render(muxy.data);
muxy.onDataChange(render);
muxy.tabs.setTitle("Report");
muxy.tabs.setIcon({ symbol: "doc.text" });   // or { svg: "..." }, or null
```

## Theme

Pages get the app's colors as CSS variables, updated live:

```css
body {
  background: var(--muxy-background);
  color: var(--muxy-foreground);
  border-color: var(--muxy-border);
}
```

Variables: `--muxy-background`, `--muxy-foreground`, `--muxy-foreground-muted`,
`--muxy-surface`, `--muxy-surface-solid`, `--muxy-border`, `--muxy-hover`,
`--muxy-accent`, `--muxy-accent-foreground`, `--muxy-accent-soft`,
`--muxy-diff-add`, `--muxy-diff-remove`, `--muxy-diff-hunk`, and
`--muxy-topbar-height`. The same values are in `muxy.theme`, with
`colorScheme` set to `light` or `dark`. `muxy.onThemeChange(fn)` reports
changes.

Muxy draws `--muxy-background` behind every page, unless a panel is
`transparent`. It shows while the page loads and wherever the page leaves its
background unset, so a page never flashes white as it opens.

## File openers

A file opener lets an extension open files that users `Cmd`-click in a
terminal, in one of its tab types.

```json
"fileOpeners": [
  { "id": "markdown", "title": "Markdown preview", "tabType": "viewer", "patterns": ["*.md"] }
]
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `tabType` | One of the extension's tab types. |
| `patterns` | Default file types, using case-insensitive `*`/`?` globs. Patterns without `/` match the filename at any depth; patterns with `/` match the project-relative path. Omitted or empty means no automatic matches. Use `["*"]` explicitly to support every file. |
| `fileTypes` | Optional automatic registrations, using the same globs. When present, overrides `patterns` in new Muxy versions, including an empty list. Older Muxy versions ignore it and use `patterns`. |
| `singleton` | Reuse one tab. Default `true`. |

Enabled extensions register these patterns automatically. One matching opener
opens the file directly. If several match, Muxy shows a searchable chooser.
The user can open once or turn on **Always use for this type** before selecting
an opener. With no matching extension, local files are revealed in Finder (or
the system file manager on Linux). Directories and files outside the project
also use the file manager. Remote files retain their remote-file actions.

**Settings → General → Files** lists registrations and lets users add custom
patterns, choose or remove defaults, reorder rules, select **Always ask** for a
pattern, or enable **Always show the file opener**. A custom rule can assign a
file type to an extension even when it is absent from the manifest's patterns.
The first matching rule with an available opener wins. Unavailable extension
rules are ignored until the extension is enabled again. The topbar project-app
picker is independent of terminal file links.

The tab receives `data` like
`{ "filePath": "docs/README.md", "line": 12, "column": 3, "source": "terminal" }`,
with `filePath` relative to the clicked file's project. Local paths are resolved
before dispatch, so symlinks must resolve inside that project. The opener
receives the resolved relative path.

### Supporting older Muxy versions

Keep the existing opener ID, tab type, `patterns`, and data contract. Add
`fileTypes` to advertise precise automatic registrations without changing how
older versions handle an explicitly selected opener:

```json
"fileOpeners": [
  {
    "id": "editor",
    "tabType": "code-editor",
    "patterns": ["*"],
    "fileTypes": ["*.md", "*.txt", "*.rs", "*.png", "*.pdf", "Dockerfile"],
    "singleton": false
  }
]
```

New Muxy versions use `fileTypes`; older versions continue using `patterns` and
their global opener preference. No new JavaScript API is required. Publish the
updated manifest schema before releasing an extension that uses the new field.

# AI Agents

Muxy recognizes AI coding agents running in its terminals and shows whether
each one is working, waiting for you, or done. It needs no setup, hooks, or
plugins, and works while no app is open.

## Supported agents

Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Droid, Grok, Hermes, Kiro,
Oh My Pi, OpenCode, Pi, and Xal.

The server spots them from the running program and what's on screen.
Recognition is best effort.

An agent that reports its own status with the
[program status protocol](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status)
(OSC 7501), such as recent Claude Code, is followed by its reports instead of
its screen. Its `app` name is enough to recognize it, so this also works over
SSH.

Oh My Pi detection reads its OSC terminal-title run state: a spinner while
working, `!` when waiting, and `>` when idle. It also recognizes optional OSC
progress reports, `⎋` working messages, and the older `Working… [esc]` spinner.
In `omp --print` sessions, a final non-empty
`Working...` line signals work; once output follows it, that progress line
no longer keeps the session busy. Detection uses terminal escape sequences
and screen text, so disabling or customizing these signals can affect recognition.

For foreground `omp` and `oh-my-pi` processes, automatic terminal titles omit
the leading `π ` prefix. The provider icon remains visible, and custom tab
titles are unchanged.

Hermes is recognized whether it was installed as a `hermes` command or by its
installer, which starts Python with a launcher program. In the TUI
(`hermes --tui`), its state comes from the window title it sets: `⏳` while
working, `⚠` while waiting, and `✓` when idle, in every language. In the
default CLI, it comes from the screen: the spinner on the line above the input
while working, and the approval, question, password, and setup prompts with
their English labels. The classic layout (`display.cli_layout: classic`) and
other languages show the CLI as idle.

## States

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Working | The agent is busy. |
| Waiting | The agent needs your input. |
| Idle | The agent is done or not doing anything. |

Tabs, worktrees, and projects show the agent's icon and state. When several
agents run, "waiting" wins.

## Notifications

The desktop app sends a macOS notification when an agent needs your attention
or finishes working.

- No notification is shown for the pane you are looking at, or for detached
  terminals.
- Looking at the terminal clears the alert in every app.
- Clicking a notification jumps to its pane.
- Only one app notifies, so alerts are never doubled.
- Turn notifications off in **System Settings → Notifications → Muxy**.

Paired phones get [push notifications](mobile.md#push-notifications) for the
same events while the Muxy app is away, about 20 seconds after they happen,
unless someone has looked at the terminal by then. Tapping one opens the
terminal on the phone.

Alerts live in memory on the server, at most one per terminal. Restarting the
server clears them.

## Agents panel

`Cmd+Opt+A` shows the agents panel, focuses it, and hides it once it has
focus. Use the arrow keys and Return to open a row.

- It sits at the bottom of the expanded sidebar; drag its top edge to make it
  taller or shorter. With the sidebar collapsed it
  opens as a popup that closes when you click elsewhere. Once you have shown
  the panel, the collapsed sidebar keeps a button for it until you hide it.
- **Move to Right** docks it in the right panel, even when the left sidebar is
  collapsed. Drag its left edge to resize it; Muxy remembers the side and width.
  It shares this area with extension panels and the panel-mode composer: opening
  one replaces the other. Use `Cmd+Opt+A` to bring Agents back. **Move to Left
  Sidebar** returns it to the sidebar.
- **Detach** floats it over the workspace. Drag its header to move it and its
  edges or corner to resize it; Muxy remembers where. **Reattach to Sidebar** or
  **Reattach to Right Panel** docks it on its last side. The other side's move
  button is also available while floating.
- **Settings → Appearance → Agents panel rows** lists each agent grouped by
  project, most urgent first, with its status on the right like its tab, where
  Return opens its pane; or each project and worktree running agents, with
  counts, where Return opens the worktree. Completed and idle agents keep their
  place, so opening a finished agent doesn't move it.
- **Settings → Appearance → Group by project** puts a heading naming each
  project above its agents. It's on by default.
- **Settings → Appearance → Agents panel density** shows each agent on two
  lines, its tab's title and then its agent and status, with its project too
  when agents aren't grouped (**Normal**), or on one short line with just its
  icon and title (**Compact**).
- **Settings → Appearance → Agents panel icon** shows each row's agent icon,
  or the icon of its project. Worktrees show their project's icon.
- **Settings → Appearance → Show project colors** marks each row with a bar of
  its project's color down its left edge. It's offered with agent icons in
  Normal rows only, since a project icon already shows its project's color
  and a compact row's icon is its only mark.
- **Settings → Appearance → Show idle time** shows how long ago each completed
  or idle agent finished, at the right of its row. After the app restarts, an
  agent whose finish you already saw shows no time until it finishes again.

## Saved agent sessions

Click the **Agent Sessions** history icon on the right of the titlebar, or use
**Toggle Agent Sessions** in the command palette or View menu, to show or hide
the right panel. It has no default shortcut; assign one in Settings → Keyboard.
This is separate from the running-agents panel.

- Sessions belong to the selected local project directory. Worktrees have their
  own history; remote projects never display this computer's sessions.
- Search matches session titles, IDs, and provider names. The filter button on
  the right of search opens a multi-select menu with matching counts,
  **Select all**, and **Clear**. Provider choices, panel visibility, and width
  are remembered.
- Sessions are grouped by recency, with the provider and age under each title.
  Use Up/Down while searching to select a session, then Return to resume it.
  Tab opens provider filtering. Escape clears the search; Escape again returns
  focus to the terminal.
- Click a session to resume it in a new project terminal using the harness's
  native resume command. The harness must be installed and available on the
  terminal's PATH. Muxy does not install, configure, or authenticate it.
- Drag the left edge to resize. The panel shares the right-panel area with
  Agents, extension panels, and the panel-mode composer; opening one replaces
  the other.
- **Pop Out Panel** in its header floats it over the workspace instead, beside
  any docked panel and other floating panels. Drag its header to move it and
  any edge or corner to resize it; **Dock Panel** puts it back. The choice and
  where it floats are remembered. Clicking a floating panel brings it to the
  front.
- History refreshes on opening the panel or switching projects. Large histories
  load automatically in bounded batches across providers; keep browsing while
  loading completes. Use **Refresh sessions** to pick up later changes.

Discovery only reads local JSONL files; it runs in the background, caches
metadata rather than conversations, and never installs hooks or launches a
harness. Files are not modified by discovery. Resuming hands control to the
harness, which may update its session normally.

| Provider | Session files | Resume command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` | `claude --resume ID` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/*.jsonl` | `codex resume ID` |
| Copilot | `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl` | `copilot --resume ID` |
| Droid | `~/.factory/sessions/*/*.jsonl` | `droid --resume ID` |
| Pi | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl` | `pi --session ID` |
| Oh My Pi | `~/.omp/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl` | `omp --resume ID` |
| Xal | `~/.xal/sessions/*/*.jsonl` | `xal resume ID` |

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME` are respected when set to absolute paths.
OpenCode, Cursor, Grok, Kiro, Antigravity, and Hermes appear as **Not
supported** in the filter menu: their database-only or unverified storage
formats are not read.
Running-agent detection for these providers is unaffected.

Session discovery is best effort: malformed or unfinished records, records
without a project directory, and nested subagent artifacts are skipped. Reads
are bounded to the start and end of transcripts; unusually large metadata,
older formats, custom storage locations, and titles in separate databases may
not be found. Sessions are sorted by transcript modification time.

## Agents Focused sidebar

Choose **Agents Focused** from the sidebar layout menu to list only the tabs
that run an agent.

## From a shell and extensions

- `muxy activity list --json` prints agent status and unread alerts as JSON.
  `muxy activity ack <event-id>` clears alerts.
- Extensions get the `agent.status` event and `muxy.agents.list()`. See
  [Events](../extensions/events.md).
- Agents can build extensions for you. See
  [Build with an agent](../extensions/agents.md).

# Browser

The desktop app has a built-in browser. A browser is a pane like a terminal,
so it opens in a tab or a split, and its page keeps running while hidden.

## Open a page

- **File → New Browser Tab** (`Cmd+Opt+B` on macOS, `Ctrl+Alt+B` on Linux), the globe button in the tab
  strip, or the command palette.
- `muxy browser open <url>` from a terminal. See [Muxy CLI](muxy-cli.md#browser-control).
- Command-click a link in a terminal, when **Settings → Browser → Open terminal
  links in the browser** is on.
- A page that opens a new window gets a new tab instead.

Type an address or a search in the address bar. Matching history shows below
it. Links to other apps, such as `mailto:`, open in those apps.

## In a page

| Action | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Address bar | `Cmd+L` | `Ctrl+L` |
| Reload | `Cmd+R` | `Ctrl+R` |
| Back / forward | `Cmd+[` / `Cmd+]` | `Alt+Left` / `Alt+Right` |
| Find on page | `Cmd+F` | `Ctrl+Shift+F` |
| Zoom in / out / reset | `Cmd+=` / `Cmd+-` / `Cmd+0` | `Ctrl+=` / `Ctrl+-` / `Ctrl+0` |
| Copy the page's address | `Cmd+Shift+C` | `Ctrl+Shift+C` |
| Web Inspector | `Cmd+Opt+I` | `Ctrl+Shift+I` |

The toolbar also opens the page in another browser and switches the tab's
profile.

## Profiles

Each profile keeps its own cookies, site data, history, and logins. New tabs use
the default profile. Manage profiles in **Settings → Browser**, where you can
also import history, bookmarks, and cookies from another browser on this
computer.

## Saved and not saved

A browser tab remembers its address and profile across restarts. Its title,
zoom, and back/forward history start fresh.

## Turning it off

Turn off **Settings → Browser → Enable built-in browser** to disable browser
tabs and `muxy browser`. Terminal links then open in your system browser.

## Linux

The browser uses WebKitGTK 4.1, version 2.42 or newer. It shares the Linux
extension renderer's [input and clipboard limits](../tech/constraints.md#experimental-linux-desktop).
Navigation, profiles, history, find, Web Inspector and CLI automation work through
this renderer, including screenshots of hidden tabs. The app still starts without
WebKitGTK installed; opening a browser reports the missing engine.
Right-click a page and choose **Web Inspector** to open developer tools, or use
`Ctrl+Shift+I`. Pages with their own context menu retain it.

Cookie import from Firefox is available on Linux. Importing encrypted Chromium
cookies requires macOS Keychain and is unavailable on Linux. Website file pickers,
JavaScript dialogs, downloads, camera, microphone and location requests are not
supported by the Linux host.

# Composer

The composer is a text box for writing long prompts and commands, with files
and images. It sends to the active terminal, or to every visible terminal in
the project. Handy for AI agents.

## Use it

| Action | Default shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Open or close | `Cmd+I` |
| Send and press Return | `Cmd+Return` |
| Send without Return | `Cmd+Shift+Return` |
| Close | `Esc` |

- Sending first clears the terminal's prompt with `Ctrl+U`, in programs that
  support it.
- With text selected, only the selection is sent.
- **Send to All Split Panes** in the **…** menu sends to every pane you can see
  in the project. If one of them isn't a live terminal, such as an extension
  tab, nothing is sent.
- A failed send keeps the draft. Some terminals may already have received it,
  so check before retrying.
- Each project keeps its own draft, saved across restarts.

## Files and images

Attach with **Attach File**, drag and drop, or paste.

- Files are inserted as quoted paths.
- Images appear as `[Image N]`. By default they are put on the clipboard and
  sent with `Ctrl+V`, which AI tools read. Set **Settings → Composer → Image
  submission** to paste file paths instead.
- For [remote](remote-servers.md) terminals, attachments are uploaded and the
  remote path is sent.

## Layout

The composer opens as a panel on the right or bottom, or as a floating box
that closes after sending. Switch from its **…** menu, which also has
**Clear After Sending**, **Clear on Close**, and **Reset Composer Size**.
`Cmd+=` and `Cmd+-` change its font size.

# Git

For Git projects, the status bar shows the branch, the changes, and pull
request state. Commits and pull requests are written by an AI command-line
tool you already have.

## Branch and changes

- **Branch:** switch, create, or delete branches.
- **Changes:** see changed files with line counts. Stage, unstage, or discard
  them, one at a time or all at once.

## Commit and push

**Commit** asks the AI for a commit message, then commits. Before it starts,
pick the AI tool, whether to include unstaged changes or only what's staged,
and whether to push. Muxy remembers these choices for next time. You can also
add one-off instructions for the AI.

## Create a pull request

**Create PR** creates a new branch, commits your changes, pushes, and opens a
pull request with an AI-written title and description. It follows the
repository's pull request template when there is one. It needs uncommitted
changes and a GitHub remote named `origin`.

When the branch has a pull request, the status bar shows its number, state,
and checks. From there you can merge (merge commit, squash, or rebase), update
it from its base branch, close it, or open it on GitHub. In a worktree, you can
also remove the worktree after merging: Muxy asks first, then switches to the
primary checkout.

Pull request features need the [`gh`](https://cli.github.com) CLI, installed and
signed in on the project's server.

## AI tools

Muxy uses the first installed of: Claude Code (`claude`), Codex (`codex`),
OpenCode (`opencode`), GitHub Copilot (`copilot`), Cursor (`cursor-agent`),
Droid (`droid`), Grok (`grok`), Kiro CLI (`kiro-cli`), Pi (`pi`), Xal (`xal`),
Antigravity (`agy`), and Oh My Pi (`omp`).

In **Settings → AI**, pick the tool for commits and for pull requests, and edit
their prompts. A project can have its own pull request prompt, set from the
**Create PR** menu.

- Sign in to the tool in a terminal first. Muxy runs it without prompts.
- The tool runs on this Mac, in the project folder. For a
  [remote project](remote-servers.md), the same folder must exist here.
- Muxy itself always does the staging, committing, pushing, and pull request.
  The AI only writes the text.

# Mobile

The Muxy phone apps connect straight to the server on your computer, with no
account. A paired phone sees the same projects and terminals as your desktop.
The one service involved is the relay at `muxy.app`, which delivers
[push notifications](#push-notifications) without being able to read them.

A phone connects in one of two ways:

- **Paired:** over your local network, a VPN such as Tailscale, or a public
  address. The connection is encrypted and the phone trusts only your server.
- **Over SSH:** the phone logs in like `muxy --host` does. No pairing or open
  port needed. See [Remote servers](remote-servers.md).

## Pair a phone

From the desktop app:

1. Open **Settings → Servers** with **Manage Servers…** in the sidebar's
   **Servers** popover. Under **Clients**, turn on **Allow
   clients**.
2. Under **Pair a client**, choose **Show Pairing Code**.
3. Scan the code with the Muxy app.

The desktop app's [welcome tour](../product/app-model.md#welcome-tour) can also
pair a phone, with **Pair a Phone** on its mobile step.

From a shell, on any computer with `muxy`:

```bash
muxy mobile enable
muxy mobile pair
```

- A pairing code works once, for five minutes, and only while it is on screen.
- The code lists your computer's addresses. If phones reach it by another name,
  such as a cloud server's public name, put it first:
  `muxy mobile pair --address devbox.example.com`.
- Phones connect on port `7419` by default. Change it in **Settings → Servers**
  or with `muxy mobile enable --port <port>`.

## Manage phones

| Task | Desktop | CLI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| See status and phones | **Clients** in **Settings → Servers** | `muxy mobile` |
| Revoke a phone | **Revoke** next to it | `muxy mobile revoke <id>` |
| Turn access off | **Allow clients** off | `muxy mobile disable` |
| Pause or resume push notifications | **Push notifications** | `muxy mobile push off\|on` |
| Reset a phone's notifications | **Reset Notifications** next to it | `muxy mobile push reset <id>` |

Revoking a phone, or turning access off, disconnects it at once.

## Push notifications

A paired phone can get a notification when an agent needs your attention or
finishes working while you're away from the Muxy app. Tapping it opens that
terminal.

- Turn them on in the Muxy app, for each computer it is paired with.
- The server waits about 20 seconds. If you look at the terminal on any device
  in that time, or the Muxy app is open and connected, nothing is sent.
- Notifications go through `muxy.app`, which forwards them to Apple or Google.
  Their content is encrypted for your phone; the relay sees only that there is
  a notification.
- They're on by default for every computer. Pause them for all phones with
  **Push notifications** under **Settings → Servers → Clients**, shown while
  **Allow clients** is on, or
  `muxy mobile push off`:
  - Nothing more is sent to `muxy.app`, which forgets the phones at once.
  - This computer keeps each phone's registration for 90 days. Turning
    notifications back on in that time resumes the phones without them
    reconnecting. After that, each phone registers again when it next
    connects.
- **Reset Notifications**, or `muxy mobile push reset <id>`, gives one phone a
  new notification key without unpairing it. Use it if you think a key leaked.
- `muxy mobile` shows whether each phone gets them, is paused, or was refused
  by Apple or Google.
- Phones connected over SSH don't get them.

## What a phone can do

A paired phone gets full terminal access: it can use projects, terminals, Git,
and files. It can't manage client access, change server settings, stop the
server, or run programs with `exec`.

Terminals opened on the phone show up as tabs in the desktop app on the same
computer.

Other computers pair with the same code's link; see
[Remote servers](remote-servers.md#pair-with-another-computer).

## Troubleshooting

- On macOS, allow `muxy-server` if the firewall asks.
- On iOS, the Muxy app needs local network permission.
- The phone and computer must reach each other: same network, a VPN, or an
  address added with `--address`.
- No push notifications: check they're on in the Muxy app and on the computer
  (`muxy mobile`). The computer must reach `https://muxy.app`, directly or
  through the proxy in `HTTPS_PROXY`. "Refused by Apple or Google" means the
  phone should get a new token: turn notifications off and on in the app.

# Muxy CLI

The `muxy` command talks to the [server](server.md) from a shell. It manages
projects, terminal sessions, worktrees, server settings, and phone access. No
desktop app is needed, so it works on Linux and over SSH too.

Commands work with what the server owns: projects and sessions. Tabs, panes, and
workspaces belong to each app, so there are no commands for them. Browser tabs
are the exception: they live in the desktop app, and `muxy browser` talks to
the app on this computer. The [terminal UI](terminal-ui.md) is an app of its
own, with its own layout.

## Install

- **With the desktop app:** choose **Install Command Line Tool…** from the app
  menu. It links `~/.local/bin/muxy` to the copy inside the app.
- **On its own:** see [Getting started](../user-guide/getting-started.md#cli-and-server-only).

Make sure `~/.local/bin` is on your `PATH`.

## Basics

```bash
muxy                 # open the terminal UI
muxy .               # open this folder in the desktop app or the terminal UI
muxy project list    # list projects
muxy ls              # list live terminal sessions
muxy --help          # grouped command overview
muxy help session send  # help for one subcommand
```

- Commands start the server they use if it isn't running, including a remote
  one with `--host`. `muxy server status` and `muxy server stop` never start
  it.
- Management commands take `--json` for machine-readable output, except
  `muxy mobile`. Existing JSON shapes are unchanged.
- On a terminal, lists have headers and aligned columns, or labeled records
  when the terminal is too narrow. Empty lists explain what is missing.
  Piped output keeps the original formats: TSV lists, JSON server/settings
  output, and bare IDs from creation commands. Terminal captures and program
  output remain unformatted. `NO_COLOR=1` disables help and table colors.
- `project list`, `session list`, and `worktree list` accept `--quiet` (`-q`)
  for one ID per line. Worktree lists omit unregistered worktrees in this mode.
  `--quiet` cannot be combined with `--json`.
- Ending or discarding a session and deleting a project or worktree need
  `--yes`.
- A project can be named by its ID, its name if unique, or its folder.
- `--host <destination>` runs the command against the server on another
  computer. It must come first: `muxy --host devbox project list`. See
  [Remote servers](remote-servers.md).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `muxy` | Opens the [terminal UI](terminal-ui.md). |
| `muxy <folder>` | Opens a new terminal in the folder's project in the desktop app, adding the project if needed. Over SSH, or without the desktop app, opens it in the terminal UI. |
| `muxy server start\|status\|stop` | Starts, inspects, or stops the server. `stop` refuses while terminals run; add `--force` to end them. |
| `muxy project list\|inspect\|add\|rename\|set-color\|set-icon\|delete` | Manages projects. Deleting ends its terminals but keeps files on disk. |
| `muxy session list\|inspect\|rename\|create\|send\|send-keys\|read-screen\|history\|search\|wait\|end\|discard\|show` | Creates and names terminals, inspects live or saved sessions, sends input, reads output, waits for text or exit, and shows a terminal in the desktop app. |
| `muxy worktree list\|create\|checkout-pr\|register\|remove` | Manages Git worktree projects, including checking out pull requests. |
| `muxy settings get\|set` | Reads or changes [server settings](server.md#settings). |
| `muxy config list\|get\|set\|unset\|reload` | Reads or changes the desktop app's settings on this computer and applies them to the running app. See [App settings](#app-settings). |
| `muxy activity list\|ack` | Reads or clears [AI agent](ai-agents.md) activity. |
| `muxy browser open\|list\|read\|click\|…` | Drives browser tabs in the desktop app on this computer. See [Browser control](#browser-control). |
| `muxy extension list\|status\|logs\|load\|enable\|disable\|reload\|unload\|validate\|publish\|dev\|pages\|open\|run\|emit\|page` | Manages, develops, and tests extensions in the desktop app on this computer. See [Extension commands](#extension-commands). |
| `muxy status <state> [--app APP] [--msg TEXT]` | Tells the terminal what a script is doing (OSC 7501): `idle`, `working`, `done`, `blocked`, `error`, or `clear`. Needs no server. |
| `muxy exec <project> -- <program> [args]` | Runs a program in the project folder, without a shell. |
| `muxy git`, `muxy files` | Run raw server Git and file actions as JSON. Advanced; the JSON shape follows the protocol and may change. |
| `muxy mobile` | Turns on phone access, pairs phones, and pauses or resumes push notifications with `muxy mobile push off\|on`, and resets one phone's with `muxy mobile push reset <id>`. See [Mobile](mobile.md). |
| `muxy install-skills` | Installs the Muxy CLI skill for the AI agents found in your home folder. `--dir <path>` adds another skills folder. |
| `muxy stdio` | Joins stdin and stdout to the server. Used by `--host` over SSH; you don't run it yourself. |

## Short commands and shell completion

These aliases accept exactly the same arguments as their longer forms:

| Alias | Full command |
| --- | --- |
| `muxy ls` | `muxy session list` |
| `muxy new` | `muxy session create` |
| `muxy send` | `muxy session send` |
| `muxy send-key` | `muxy session send-keys` |
| `muxy capture` | `muxy session read-screen` |
| `muxy wait` | `muxy session wait` |

`muxy help session create` and `muxy session create --help` show the same
command-specific usage. Running a management group without a subcommand
shows its help. Help, version and completions never connect to a server.
Use `./ls`, for example, to open a folder named like an alias.

Generate completions for command names, nested subcommands and options:

```bash
eval "$(muxy completion bash)"  # Bash
source <(muxy completion zsh)   # Zsh, after autoload -Uz compinit; compinit
muxy completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/muxy.fish
```

Add the appropriate eval or source line to your shell startup file. Completions use
this installed CLI's command catalog, not a running server, and do not fetch
live project or session IDs.

## Extension commands

These talk to the desktop app on this computer and start it if needed, so they
don't take `--host`. [Agents building extensions](../extensions/agents.md) use
them too.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `muxy extension list [--json]` | Lists extensions with their version, state, source, and folder, then any load errors. |
| `muxy extension status <name> [--json]` | Shows one extension, its load errors, and recent log lines. |
| `muxy extension logs <name> [--lines N]` | Prints recent log lines. The default is 100. |
| `muxy extension load <folder>` | Loads an unpacked folder, disabled. Loading a folder that is already loaded reloads it. |
| `muxy extension enable <name>`, `disable <name>` | Turns an extension on or off. |
| `muxy extension reload <name>` | Restarts one extension from its folder. If the folder no longer loads, or its package name changed, it prints why and the running copy stays. |
| `muxy extension unload <name>` | Forgets an unpacked folder and keeps its files. It doesn't work on marketplace extensions. |
| `muxy extension validate <name\|folder> [--json]` | Checks what publishing needs, including the GitHub CLI, and exits nonzero if something is missing. |
| `muxy extension publish <name> [--json]` | Opens a [pull request to the store](../extensions/contributing.md#publish-from-muxy), after you approve it in the app. |

### Developing and testing

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `muxy extension dev <folder> [--once]` | Loads and turns on an unpacked folder, then builds it (`npm run build`, or the package manager its lock file names) and reloads it whenever its files change. Each round prints `ready` or `failed` with the log lines it added. `--once` does one round and exits nonzero if it failed. |
| `muxy extension pages <name> [--json]` | Lists the extension's open pages: page ID, kind, ID, panel instance, whether it loaded, whether it shows, and its title. |
| `muxy extension open <name> panel:<id>\|tab:<type>\|modal:<entry> [--data JSON]` | Opens a panel, tab, or modal page, waits for it to load, and prints its page ID. |
| `muxy extension run <name> <command>` | Runs one of the extension's commands, as the command palette does. |
| `muxy extension emit <name> <event> [payload]` | Sends the extension an event its manifest lists, with a JSON object payload, to test how it reacts. |
| `muxy extension page <action> <page-id> …` | Drives a page with the [browser](#browser-control) page actions: `read`, `screenshot [--out FILE]`, `eval`, `click`, `type`, `fill`, `press`, `select`, `hover`, `scroll-into-view`, `check`, `uncheck`, `is`, `wait`, `wait-for`, `get-text`, `get-html`, `get-value`, `get-attribute`, `get-count`, `find`, `snapshot`, and `storage get\|set\|clear`. |

```bash
muxy extension dev extensions/hello --once
page=$(muxy extension open hello panel:hello)
muxy extension page snapshot "$page"
muxy extension page click "$page" "#hi"
muxy extension page wait "$page" --text "Sent"
muxy extension page screenshot "$page" --out hello.png
```

A call that needs the user to answer a [runtime prompt](../extensions/permissions.md#runtime-prompts)
waits for them: the extension's log says so, and `status` counts the prompts
still waiting. Nothing here answers them or changes what an extension may do.

## App settings

```bash
muxy config list                          # every setting, defaults included
muxy config get terminal                  # one table, as TOML
muxy config set appearance.dark_theme "Builtin Dark"
muxy config set terminal.font_size 14
muxy config set 'keymap."settings.focus_navbar"' cmd-l
muxy config unset terminal.font_size
muxy config reload                        # apply hand edits
```

- Keys are dotted paths in `settings.toml`, or in `terminal.toml` after
  `terminal.`. Quote a part that holds a dot. New settings get keys
  automatically, from the files' own format. Optional settings appear in
  `list` once they are set.
- Values are TOML, such as `true`, `14`, or `["Menlo", "Monaco"]`. Anything else
  is text, so names need no quotes of their own.
- A change is saved only if the app can still start with it, and the file is
  left as it was otherwise. `set` and `unset` then have a running desktop app
  apply it. They never start the app, which reads the files when it starts.
- Remote servers are read-only here; manage them in **Settings → Devices**.
  Server settings use `muxy settings`.
- `config` works on this computer's profile and doesn't take `--host`. Every
  command takes `--json` for machine-readable output.

## Sessions from a script

```bash
id=$(muxy session create my-app)
muxy session send "$id" "npm test"
muxy session send-keys "$id" Enter
muxy session read-screen "$id" --lines 20
muxy session end "$id" --yes
```

- `send` types text without pressing Return. `send --stdin` reads piped or
  redirected input verbatim, including newlines; it accepts up to 1 MiB and
  sends nothing if input exceeds that limit. It cannot also take a text argument.
- `send-keys` sends one or more keys in order: `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`,
  `Backspace`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+D`, or `Ctrl+Z`. All keys are validated before
  any input is sent.
- `read-screen` returns the last visible rows. `history` and `search` page
  through scrollback as JSON.
- `--saved` reads a session's last saved screen, even after it ended.
- `end` stops the program and keeps its saved output. `discard` also deletes
  the output.
- Sessions created here outlive the command and appear in every app under
  **Existing Terminals**.
- `show` opens a session in a new tab of its project in the desktop app on
  this computer, starting it if needed. When a tab already shows the session,
  `show` selects that tab instead. It never brings a running app to the front.
  With `--background`, `show` adds the tab without switching to it.
- Inside a Muxy terminal, session commands default to that terminal, and
  `create` to its project.
- `create` can take a `--directory` and a command to run after `--`.
- `wait --text <text>` waits for text on the screen, and `wait --exit` for the
  shell to exit. Both give up after 30 seconds by default.

### Inspect and name sessions

```bash
muxy project inspect my-app
muxy session inspect "$id" --json
muxy session rename "$id" dev-server
muxy ls --project my-app --quiet
printf 'npm test\n' | muxy send "$id" --stdin
muxy send-key "$id" Ctrl+C Enter
```

Inspection includes a session's name, status, project, directory and owner,
including saved sessions. Renaming uses the server's shared name, so every
connected app sees it. Names must be nonempty, trimmed, at most 256 bytes and
contain no control characters. Existing session commands continue to target
numeric IDs; renaming does not change the ID. Older servers without session
naming report that the operation is unsupported.

## Browser control

```bash
tab=$(muxy browser open localhost:3000)
muxy browser wait-for-navigation "$tab"
muxy browser fill "$tab" "#email" "me@example.com"
muxy browser click "$tab" "button[type=submit]"
muxy browser wait "$tab" --text "Welcome"
muxy browser read "$tab"
muxy browser screenshot "$tab" --out page.png
muxy browser close "$tab"
```

- Browser commands need the desktop app and don't take `--host`. `open` starts
  the app if it isn't running.
- `open` prints the new tab's ID. Pass it to the other commands.
- `snapshot` lists a page's interactive elements, each with a selector for
  `click`, `fill`, or `type`.
- `muxy browser --help` lists every command.

## Exit codes

`0` on success. On any error, `muxy` prints `muxy: <message>` to stderr and exits
with `1`, including when a program run with `muxy exec` fails.

## Profiles

`MUXY_DIR` points the CLI, and the server it starts, at another profile folder.
Use it to run a separate, throwaway server. See [Server](server.md#files).

# Projects

A project is a folder on a server. You work in its tabs, and its terminals
belong to it. Projects are shared by every app on that server; tabs, splits,
workspaces, and project order are kept by each app.

## Projects

- Add one with **Add Project** below the project list or in the sidebar's filter
  menu when focused on one project, **File → Open Project…**, or `Cmd+O`. Type to search folders, type a
  path, or choose **Finder…** (**Browse…** on Linux) to pick a folder in the
  system dialog. Each server's **Add Project** adds to that server, and
  `Cmd+O` to the current project's. On another computer's server, browse its
  folders or type a path there instead; Finder and Browse only reach this
  computer.
- `muxy <folder>` in a shell opens a terminal in that folder's project in the
  desktop app, adding the project if needed. On macOS, so does dropping a folder
  on the Dock icon or using **Open With**.
- Right-click a project to rename it, or change its icon, logo, or color.
- Projects automatically use a favicon or logo from their folder when no custom
  icon or logo is set. Muxy checks the root first, then common folders such as
  `public`, `static`, `app`, `src/app`, `src/assets`, and `assets`. It supports
  SVG, ICO, PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, and ICNS up to 5 MiB each, including projects on
  remote servers.
  Icons refresh when you return to Muxy, and a remote project's when its server
  connects again; unreadable images fall back to the usual project tile. Home keeps its built-in icon.
- **Remove Project…** removes it from every app and ends its terminals. Files
  stay on disk.
- **Add Project → Recently Removed** brings back one of the last 10 removed
  projects with its name, icon, and color.
- If a project's folder disappears, it shows as missing and can only be
  removed.

**Home** is the built-in project for your home folder. It is always first and
can't be removed. `Cmd+N` opens a tab in Home.

## Sidebar

- `Cmd+B` shows or hides the sidebar.
- Pick a layout from the sidebar header:
  - **Project Focused** (default): projects, with worktrees under them.
  - **Tab Focused**: projects with their tabs listed in the sidebar.
  - **Agents Focused**: only tabs running an [AI agent](ai-agents.md).
- In Tab Focused and Agents Focused, projects without tabs hide behind **N more
  projects** at the bottom. Turn on **Settings → Appearance → Remember shown
  projects without tabs** to keep them shown after a restart.
- Sort by **Manual Order** and drag to reorder, or by **Name**.
- Drop a dragged tab or pane on a project to move it there as a new tab. See
  [Moving tabs and panes](../product/app-model.md#moving-tabs-and-panes).
- `Ctrl+1`–`Ctrl+9` jumps to a project. Hold a modifier to see the numbers.

## Workspaces

A workspace is a named filter for the sidebar. Create one from the workspace
menu in the sidebar header. Add projects from a project's **Workspaces** menu.
A project can be in any number of workspaces. Deleting a workspace never
removes its projects.

## Worktrees

For Git projects, worktrees appear under their project and have their own
tabs. Turn them on with **Worktrees → Show Worktrees** in the project menu.
Worktrees created outside Muxy show up on their own.

**Switch Worktree…** (`Cmd+Opt+W`) lists the current project and its
worktrees: the current one first, then the most recently used, so `Down` and
Return goes back to the previous one. Type to filter, then press Return to
switch. Each worktree can be renamed or removed from its row, and **New
Worktree…** sits at the bottom. Turn off **Settings → Appearance → Order the
worktree switcher by recent use** to list them in sidebar order.

**New Worktree…** (`Cmd+Opt+N`, from the current project or worktree) asks
for:

- A name, and a new branch (from a base branch) or an existing one.
- A location: **Default** (`~/.muxy/worktrees/<project>/<name>`), a
  **Template**, or a **Folder**. Templates must contain `{branch}` and can use
  `{base-dir}` and `{project-name}`, for example `../{base-dir}.{branch}`.
  Set the default in **Settings → General**; each project remembers its choice.

**Remove Worktree and Files…** deletes the worktree folder and its project, and
ends its terminals. Muxy warns about uncommitted changes.

### Setup and teardown commands

Muxy can run commands when it creates or removes a worktree. List them in
`.muxy/worktree.json` in the project, or for every project in
`~/.config/muxy/worktree.json` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/muxy/worktree.json`):

```json
{
  "setup": ["npm ci", { "name": "Start services", "command": "docker compose up -d" }],
  "teardown": ["docker compose down"]
}
```

- Muxy shows the commands and runs them only if you turn them on in the dialog.
- Setup runs your own commands first, then the project's. Teardown runs the
  project's first.
- Commands run in the worktree with `MUXY_PROJECT_PATH`, `MUXY_WORKTREE_ID`,
  `MUXY_WORKTREE_PATH`, `MUXY_WORKTREE_NAME`, and `MUXY_WORKTREE_BRANCH`. They
  share a five-minute limit.
- A failed setup keeps the new worktree. A failed teardown stops the removal.

## Layouts

Check a `.muxy/layouts/` folder into a project to open a ready-made set of
split terminals. See [Layouts](../layouts/overview.md).

# Remote Servers Muxy can work with projects on other computers over SSH, or by [pairing](#pair-with-another-computer) with them. Each computer runs its own `muxy-server`, so remote terminals keep running when you disconnect, just like local ones. Remote projects sit in the same sidebar as local ones, under their server's heading. ```mermaid flowchart LR APP["Desktop app or muxy"] -->|"SSH · muxy stdio"| REMOTE["muxy-server
on the other computer"] ``` ## Requirements - SSH access to the computer with your keys, agent, or certificates. The desktop app also supports password logins. - A trusted host key. Run `ssh ` once to accept it. - Muxy [installed there](../user-guide/getting-started.md#cli-and-server-only), on `PATH` or in `~/.local/bin`, at a version that speaks the same protocol as yours. - macOS 14 or newer, or Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer, on x86_64 or ARM64. On Linux hosts that end your processes when you log out, run `loginctl enable-linger` so the server keeps running after SSH disconnects. ## In the desktop app 1. Open the **Servers** section at the bottom of the sidebar and choose **Add Server…**. 2. Enter the SSH host (a host name, address, or `~/.ssh/config` alias), and optionally the user, port, and identity file. 3. Choose **Test Connection**. If Muxy isn't installed there, the app offers to install the same version into `~/.local/bin`. 4. Expand it in the sidebar, then add projects with its **Add Project → Folder…**, which browses its folders. - Servers start disconnected each time Muxy opens, and their projects show what was last known. Opening one of a server's projects or tabs, expanding it in the sidebar before its projects are known, or **Connect** in its menu connects it. So does renaming or removing one of its projects, which waits for it. A server you add or pair connects right away. Its terminals that have nothing to show yet say it is disconnected, with **Connect**. - Passwords are asked when connecting and kept only in memory until you quit. - A connected server that drops reconnects on its own, waiting longer each time. It stops retrying when it needs you, for example for a password or a new host key. - Right-click a server in the **Servers** popover for its actions, or hover it and use its pencil to edit it. - Put servers in a **Group** from **Add Server…** or **Edit…**, or with **Move to Group** in their menu. The popover and **Settings → Servers** list them by group. In `settings.toml`, it is `group = "…"`. - **Manage Servers…** opens **Settings → Servers**. Under **Other Servers** it has every server by group: - Tick servers' boxes, or **Select all**, to act on several; `Shift`-click a box to tick a range. The bar above the list connects, disconnects, regroups, or forgets the ticked servers, and so does right-clicking one. - Each group heading connects its servers, and renames or deletes the group. Deleting a group keeps its servers. - **Disconnect** hangs up without ending terminals there. The server stays disconnected until you connect it or open one of its projects. - **Forget** a server to remove it and its projects from this app. Nothing on the server changes. - The status bar shows the current project's server, with connect, restart, and stop. ### In the sidebar The sidebar lists every server under its own heading: **This Mac** (**This Computer** on Linux) first, then the others in the Servers popover's order. Each heading shows how its server is doing, and clicking it expands or collapses that server's Home, projects, and **Add Project** row. This computer starts expanded and the others collapsed, and the app remembers each choice, also after a restart. Opening something on a collapsed server, such as from **New Tab in Project…**, expands it, and expanding a server that hasn't listed its projects yet connects to it. Workspaces filter the projects under every heading, and **Focus Current Project** shows only the current project, without headings. To list only this computer's projects, turn off **Settings → Appearance → Show other servers in the sidebar**; the Servers button still manages the others, and **New Tab in Project…** still offers their projects. Nothing switches the app between servers. **Add Project** adds to its own server; ⌘O and **New Tab in Project…** browse the current project's server, and the latter also offers every server's projects and the other servers by name. Terminals that another client, such as a phone or the terminal UI, shows on this computer's server open here as tabs in their project, without taking focus. Terminals other clients show on another computer's server, and those nobody shows, such as detached ones, stay in **Existing Terminals**. Closing or detaching one here leaves it running for the clients still showing it, and the app doesn't open it here again. It stays in **Existing Terminals** to open it again. ### Pair with another computer Pairing needs no SSH setup, only Muxy on both computers, macOS or Linux, which can reach each other on the network or through a VPN. 1. On the other computer, open **Settings → Servers** (**Manage Servers…** in the sidebar's **Servers** popover). Under **Clients**, turn on **Allow clients**, choose **Show Pairing Code**, then **Copy Link**. 2. Here, in the **Servers** popover or **Settings → Servers**, choose **Pair with Link…** and paste it. The paired computer works like any remote server, except that it can't be restarted from here. This computer is listed under **Clients** in the other computer's **Settings → Servers**, where **Revoke** disconnects it. If it was revoked or reset, paste a new link in its **Edit…** form to pair again. ### Custom SSH commands If a VM manager or another tool handles SSH for you, turn on **Custom command** in **Add Server…** (or **Edit…**) and enter its command prefix, for example: ```text swiftvm ssh my-vm ``` Muxy runs that local program directly and appends its remote command as **one argument**. The prefix must include the target machine and any flags or `--` separator your tool needs. Muxy does not add SSH flags, a host, or a port in this mode. The same prefix is used for Test Connection, installation, normal connections, and reconnects. - The tool must accept a remote shell command as its last argument and relay stdin/stdout unchanged **without allocating a TTY**. Interactive-shell-only tools are not supported. Add your tool's non-interactive/no-TTY flags if needed. - Authentication and host-key verification belong to the tool. Set them up in a terminal first; Muxy's password and identity-file controls do not apply here. - Single/double quotes and backslashes group arguments, so paths and VM names can contain spaces. Shell variables, `~`, wildcards, pipelines, redirects, aliases, and command substitutions are not expanded. Use an absolute program path if the tool is not on the desktop app's `PATH`. - Only configure commands you trust: they run locally with your permissions on connection and reconnection. Do not put passwords or tokens in the command; it is saved in plain text in `settings.toml`. For tools with a different argument convention, use an executable wrapper script that accepts the last argument as the remote command and forwards it without changing stdin/stdout. The remote computer still needs Muxy and the same OS requirements listed above. A custom-command entry in `settings.toml` uses `ssh_command` instead of `ssh`: ```toml [[servers]] id = "6f9619ff-8b86-4011-b42d-00c04fc964ff" # use a unique UUID name = "Development VM" ssh_command = "swiftvm ssh my-vm" ``` ## From a shell Put `--host` first to use another computer's server: ```bash muxy --host devbox # terminal UI muxy --host devbox project list # any CLI command muxy --host ssh://me@devbox:2222 # with a user and port ``` `--host` takes `user@host`, an `~/.ssh/config` alias, or `ssh://user@host:port`. It never prompts, so use a key or an agent. Folder arguments must be absolute paths on that computer. ## Working with remote files - Files dropped or pasted into a remote terminal, or sent from the [composer](composer.md), are uploaded and their remote path is pasted. - `Cmd`-clicking a remote file offers a read-only copy on this Mac, or its path. - Git runs on the server. Pull request features need `gh` installed and signed in there. - AI commit and pull request actions run on this Mac, so they only work when the project's folder also exists here. ## Updating Muxy never updates a remote computer by itself. When versions can't talk, the app shows the command to run there. To update by hand, follow the [installation instructions](../user-guide/getting-started.md#cli-and-server-only) on that computer with `--replace`, choosing the same channel and a compatible version.

# Server

`muxy-server` runs every terminal. The desktop app, the terminal UI, the CLI,
and phones are all clients of it. That is why terminals keep running after you
quit an app, and why several apps can show the same terminal.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DESKTOP["Desktop app"] <--> SERVER["muxy-server"]
    TUI["muxy terminal UI"] <--> SERVER
    CLI["muxy CLI"] <--> SERVER
    PHONE["Phone"] <--> SERVER
```

## Lifetime

- Apps and CLI commands start the server when they need it. You never need to
  start it yourself.
- It keeps running until you stop it, even with no app open.
- Stopping or restarting it ends every terminal. Saved screens and history are
  kept. Use the status bar, **Settings → Servers**, or
  `muxy server stop --force`.
- Muxy never restarts it on its own while terminals are running. After an
  update, the desktop app replaces this computer's server once no terminals are
  running.

## Sessions

- A session is one running terminal. It belongs to the project it was created
  in, wherever you `cd` later.
- It ends when its program exits, when someone ends it, or when the server
  stops. Closing the last pane that shows it ends it too.
- Quitting an app, detaching, a crash, or sleep never ends it.
- Any number of apps can show and type into a session at once. They share one
  size.
- **Existing Terminals** lists a project's sessions that this app isn't
  showing, and which app owns each one, so you can open them here too.

## History

- The server saves each terminal's screen and scrollback to disk, even when no
  app is watching. It is still there after the program ends or the server
  restarts.
- Scrollback size is a byte budget per terminal, 16 MiB by default. Older
  history loads as you scroll.
- Ended sessions and their saved output are removed after 7 days.

## Settings

Server settings apply to everyone using that server. Change them in
**Settings → Servers**, with `muxy settings set`, or in `server.toml`:

| Setting | `server.toml` key | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default shell | `default_shell` | `$SHELL`, else `/bin/zsh` on macOS and `/bin/sh` on Linux |
| History budget per session | `history_budget_bytes` | `16777216` (16 MiB) |
| Shell integration | `shell_integration` | `true` |

Shells start as login shells. Changes apply to new terminals. A new history
budget applies to saved history after the server restarts.

## Shell integration

Shell integration lets Muxy track each terminal's folder, jump between prompts,
and select a command's output. It loads automatically for zsh and fish, without
editing your startup files.

Bash is opt-in. Add this to the file your Bash profile loads for interactive
shells:

```bash
if [[ ${MUXY_SHELL_INTEGRATION:-0} == 1 ]]; then
    source "$MUXY_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR/muxy.bash"
fi
```

Every terminal gets `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`,
`TERM_PROGRAM=muxy`, `MUXY_SERVER_ID`, and `MUXY_SESSION_ID`. If `LANG`,
`LC_ALL`, and `LC_CTYPE` are all unset or empty, Muxy sets `LANG` to an
installed UTF-8 locale for the system language and region, or else `C.UTF-8` or
`en_US.UTF-8`, so non-ASCII text displays correctly. If none of these is
installed, it leaves them unset.

## Files

Everything lives in one profile folder:

| Platform | Stable | Beta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/Muxy 2` | `~/Library/Application Support/Muxy Beta` |
| Linux | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/muxy`, or `~/.local/state/muxy` | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/muxy-beta`, or `~/.local/state/muxy-beta` |

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `server.toml` | Server settings |
| `server.log` | Server log |
| `server.sock` | The socket apps connect to |
| `sessions/` | Projects, sessions, and saved terminal output |
| `remote.json` | Mobile access settings, paired phones, and their push notification registrations |
| `settings.toml`, `terminal.toml`, `themes/` | Desktop app settings, see [Settings](../user-guide/settings.md) |
| `tui-state.json` | Terminal UI layouts |

Set `MUXY_DIR` to use a different profile folder. Development builds use
`Muxy Dev` (`muxy-dev` on Linux), so they never touch your real data.

# Terminal UI

Run `muxy` with no arguments to open Muxy inside any terminal. It shows the
same projects and terminals as the desktop app, with its own tabs and splits.
It works on macOS and Linux, locally or over SSH.

```bash
muxy                   # this computer's server
muxy --host devbox     # the server on another computer, over SSH
```

## Keys

Every command starts with the prefix `Ctrl-B`, like tmux. Press `Ctrl-B ?` for
help.

| After `Ctrl-B` | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `c` | New tab in the project folder |
| `n` / `p` | Next / previous tab |
| `1`–`9`, `0` | Go to tabs 1–9, or tab 10 |
| `%` | Split side by side |
| `"` | Split top and bottom |
| Arrows | Move focus between panes |
| `Ctrl` + Arrows | Resize the split |
| `r` | Enter resize mode; use arrows, then `Esc` to leave |
| `o` / `Tab` | Next pane |
| `z` | Zoom the pane |
| `x` | Close the pane |
| `s` | Switch project |
| `(` / `)` | Previous / next project |
| `b` | Toggle the sidebar |
| `m` | Toggle mouse support |
| `[` | Enter scrollback |
| `w` | Open an existing terminal of this project |
| `d` | Detach and quit; terminals keep running |
| `Ctrl-B` | Send `Ctrl-B` to the terminal |

## Behavior

- The first run opens one shell in Home. After that, it restores your layout.
- Several `muxy` windows share one layout, and changes in one show in the
  others.
- Quitting or detaching never ends a terminal. Closing a pane ends its terminal
  unless another app still shows it, and asks first if a program is running.
- With `--host`, the layout for that server is kept on this computer.
- A tab holds up to 16 panes, and a project up to 64 tabs.
- The sidebar shows AI agent activity.

## Mouse and scrollback

Click to focus a pane or pick a project or tab, and drag a divider to resize.
Drag across text to select it; it is copied on release. Double-click selects a
word and triple-click a line. Right-click opens a menu. When a program uses the
mouse, hold `Shift` to select.

`Ctrl-B [` or `Ctrl-B PageUp` opens scrollback. Scroll with the arrows,
`PageUp`, and `PageDown`; `q` or `Esc` returns to the live screen. The mouse
wheel scrolls history too, unless the program uses the mouse or fills the
screen; then hold `Shift`.

## Not supported

The terminal UI has no custom key bindings or
[project layouts](../layouts/overview.md), and doesn't show images in the
terminal. Desktop and terminal UI layouts are kept separately.

# Terminal

Muxy's terminals run in the [server](server.md), powered by
[Ghostty](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty). They keep running after you
quit the app, and every app shows the same screen and history.

## Tabs and splits

| Action | Default shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| New tab | `Cmd+T` |
| New tab in Home | `Cmd+N` |
| Split right / down | `Cmd+D` / `Cmd+Shift+D` |
| Move focus between panes | `Cmd+Opt+Arrows` |
| Zoom the pane | `Cmd+Shift+Return` |
| Close pane / tab | `Cmd+W` / `Cmd+Shift+W` |
| Next / previous tab | `Cmd+]` / `Cmd+[` |
| Go to tab 1–9 | `Cmd+1`–`Cmd+9` |

- Every terminal pane has a header with its icon (an agent's own icon while one
  runs there) and title. At a prompt, the header names the shell, such as
  `zsh`, rather than the folder, unless the shell sets its own title. Beside
  the title, dimmed, the header shows the folder the terminal works in, such as
  `~/Projects/muxy`, unless the title already shows it. The focused pane, or
  the one under the pointer, shows buttons there to split it right or down,
  float it, maximize it, or close it.
  Drag a pane by its title to move it, as with `Cmd`-drag.
  A terminal's header takes the background a full-screen app paints its screen
  in, so it blends with the app. Turn headers off with **Settings → Appearance
  → Show pane headers**.
- Panes that aren't focused are dimmed, and the focused pane's tab is
  underlined.
- New tabs and panes open in the project folder. Turn on **Settings → Terminal →
  Keep working directory** to open them in the focused pane's folder instead. A
  new tab in another project still opens in that project's folder.
- Drag dividers to resize, or even them out with **Equalize Splits**
  (`Cmd+Ctrl+=`, or a pane's right-click menu). `Cmd`-drag a pane onto another
  pane to swap them, or onto an edge to dock it there.
- Right-click a tab to rename, color, or pin it. Pinned tabs stay first and
  can't be closed until unpinned.

See [Keyboard shortcuts](../user-guide/keyboard-shortcuts.md) for the full
list.

## Floating terminals

A terminal can float over the workspace in a panel of its own, like a small
window inside Muxy.

- **Float Pane** in a terminal's pane header, its right-click menu, or the
  command palette floats it. A pane alone in its tab takes its tab along. Only terminals float.
- Drag the empty part of the pane headers along the panel's top to move it,
  and its edges or corners to resize it. With pane headers turned off, the
  panel has a bar of its own to drag. Clicking a panel brings it to the front.
  Muxy remembers where each one sits.
- A floating terminal belongs to its project and starts out showing only while
  that project is selected. The scope button in its pane header (a folder, or
  a globe once it shows everywhere), **Show in All Projects** in its
  right-click menu, or the command palette keeps it over every project
  instead; **Show Only in** the project goes back.
- Inside a floating panel, `Cmd+D` and `Cmd+Shift+D` split it, and its panes
  move by their titles or with `Cmd`-drag into other tabs, onto the tab bar,
  or into another project, as in a tab window. Terminal panes dragged onto it
  dock there.
- **Dock as Tab** in its pane header or right-click menu puts it back among its
  project's tabs. **Move to New Window** gives it a window of its own, and
  **Float Pane** floats a tab window's terminal back over the main window.
- **Minimize** (the minus button) collapses a floating terminal into a pill at
  the bottom right of the window. Click its icon and title to restore it to its
  previous size and position. Its splits and terminals stay running. Minimized
  terminals follow their project scope; scroll the row when it fills up.
- **Toggle Floating Terminals** (`Cmd+Opt+F`, or the View menu) hides every
  floating terminal and shows them again. Hidden terminals keep running.
  Clicking a notification for a hidden one shows it.
- Floating terminals, where they sit, and whether they are hidden or minimized
  come back after a restart. Toggling floating terminals preserves minimization;
  clicking a notification for a minimized terminal restores it.

## Closing and detaching

- Closing a pane ends its terminal, unless another pane in any app still shows
  it.
- Muxy asks first when a program other than the shell is running.
- **Detach Terminal** in the pane's right-click menu removes the pane but keeps
  the terminal running.
- **Existing Terminals** (`Cmd+Opt+T`, or the project menu) lists the project's
  terminals that this app isn't showing, with the app that owns each, and opens
  one in a new tab.
- Set **Settings → General → When closing tabs or panes** to **Detach** to make
  every tab and pane close a detach.
- Quitting the app or closing its window never ends a terminal. **End All
  Sessions and Quit** in the app menu ends every terminal on this computer,
  without asking first.

## Find

`Cmd+F` searches the focused terminal, including all of its history. `Return`
or `Cmd+G` goes to the next match, `Cmd+Shift+G` to the previous. Search is
plain text and case-insensitive; **Aa** makes it case-sensitive.

## Copy and paste

- `Cmd+C` copies the selection. `Ctrl+C` goes to the program.
- Turn on **Settings → Terminal → Copy on select** to copy when you select.
- When a program uses the mouse, hold `Shift` to select text or open the
  right-click menu.
- Pasting an image into a local terminal sends `Ctrl+V`, so AI tools can read
  it from the clipboard.

## Insert a path

**Insert Path…** (`Cmd+Ctrl+I`, or the command palette) opens a list of the
files and folders in the terminal's folder, right at the cursor, and types the
path of the one you pick.

- Type to filter by name, ignoring case. Names that start with a dot show once
  the filter starts with one.
- `Up` and `Down` move through the list. `Return` types the selected row's
  path and closes the list. Nothing is run: Return is never sent for you.
- `Tab` opens the selected folder. So does typing its name and a `/`, and you
  can type `../`, `~/`, or a path from `/` to go anywhere. `Backspace` in an
  empty filter goes to the folder above.
- A path inside the terminal's folder is typed relative to it, such as
  `crates/muxy-app/Cargo.toml`. Any other is typed in full. Folders end with a
  `/`.
- Plain paths are typed as they are. A path with spaces or other special
  characters is quoted for the shell or program in the foreground, as dropped
  files are. Where it can't be quoted safely, such as inside `ssh` or `tmux`,
  it isn't typed and the list says so.
- Paths you chose recently, and the folders that hold them, are listed first
  with a clock. Muxy remembers them for each server, for all its terminals.
  Turn that off with **Settings → Terminal → Insert Path → Show recently used
  paths**.
- `Esc`, the shortcut again, or a click elsewhere closes the list.

The list follows the terminal's folder, which needs
[shell integration](server.md#shell-integration) to keep up with `cd`. On a
